properties.natural_language: The column index in a received DataColumnSidecar must be within [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS) before any further processing.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send DataColumnSidecars with arbitrary column indices via gossip subnets. Out-of-bounds index could cause array access violations or incorrect custody assignment.

properties.natural_language: The number of cells in a received DataColumnSidecar must match the expected count for the column before acceptance.

reachability.notes: Attacker can craft sidecars with incorrect cell count to cause buffer overflows or incorrect KZG verification.

properties.natural_language: The commitment_inclusion_proof in a DataColumnSidecar must be valid against the signed block header before cell KZG proofs are verified.

reachability.notes: Attacker can forge inclusion proofs to make fake commitments appear canonical. If proof verification is bypassed, fake data availability could be declared.

properties.natural_language: Each cell's KZG proof in a DataColumnSidecar must be valid against the corresponding KZG commitment before the sidecar is accepted.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send sidecars with invalid KZG proofs. If verification is flawed or skipped, fake data could be accepted as valid, breaking data availability guarantees.

properties.natural_language: After a DataColumnSidecar passes all validation (format, inclusion, KZG), it must be stored and made available for sampling and reconstruction.

reachability.notes: If validated sidecars are not properly stored, sampling and reconstruction will fail, degrading data availability.

properties.natural_language: After a DataColumnSidecar fails any validation step, the sidecar must be discarded and the sending peer must be penalized via peer scoring.

reachability.notes: If invalid sidecars are not properly rejected or peers not penalized, attackers can flood the network with invalid data without consequence.

properties.natural_language: A node's custody group assignment is deterministic: given the same node_id and custody_group_count, get_custody_groups must always return the same set of custody groups.

reachability.notes: Non-deterministic custody assignment would cause nodes to disagree on who custodies what, breaking data availability verification.

properties.natural_language: A node must always be assigned at least CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT (4) custody groups.

reachability.notes: If a node gets fewer than 4 groups, data availability sampling guarantees weaken.

properties.natural_language: The column-to-custody-group mapping must satisfy: for each custody_group g and each i in [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS/NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS), column index = NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS * i + g.

reachability.notes: Incorrect column mapping would cause nodes to subscribe to wrong subnets and miss data they are supposed to custody.

properties.natural_language: A node must be subscribed to gossip subnets for all its assigned custody groups before performing data availability sampling.

reachability.notes: If a node fails to subscribe to all custody subnets, it will miss column data and may incorrectly report data unavailability.

properties.natural_language: The number of custody groups sampled per slot must be at least max(SAMPLES_PER_SLOT, custody_group_count).

reachability.notes: Sampling fewer groups than required weakens data availability guarantees.

properties.natural_language: Column data received via Req/Resp must undergo the same validation (format, inclusion proof, KZG proofs) as data received via gossip.

reachability.notes: If Req/Resp responses bypass validation that gossip data undergoes, attackers can inject invalid columns via direct requests.

properties.natural_language: After KZG proof verification succeeds for all sampled columns, data availability must be confirmed for that slot.

reachability.notes: If sampling success is not properly propagated, the node may fail to attest, affecting consensus.

properties.natural_language: After KZG proof verification fails for any sampled column, data availability must NOT be confirmed and the node must not attest to availability.

reachability.notes: If failed sampling still results in availability attestation, invalid data can be finalized.

properties.natural_language: Matrix reconstruction via recover_matrix must only be attempted when more than 50% of columns (at least 65 of 128) are available.

reachability.notes: Attempting reconstruction with insufficient columns will produce incorrect data. The 50% threshold is mathematically required for erasure coding.

properties.natural_language: After successful matrix reconstruction, all 128 columns must be available and the reconstructed data must be consistent with the original KZG commitments.

reachability.notes: Incorrect reconstruction could produce data inconsistent with commitments, leading to invalid re-gossip.

properties.natural_language: Reconstructed columns must be treated identically to gossip-received columns in the node's data store.

reachability.notes: If reconstructed columns are not equivalent to received columns, downstream consumers may behave inconsistently.

properties.natural_language: After reconstruction, re-gossip of reconstructed columns must only occur on subnets the node is subscribed to.

reachability.notes: Re-gossiping on unsubscribed subnets could leak information or cause protocol violations.

properties.natural_language: A peer's advertised custody_group_count in ENR must be verifiable by requesting columns the peer claims to custody.

reachability.notes: Attacker can advertise false custody_group_count to appear as a super-full node but withhold data. If claims are not verified, routing decisions become unreliable.

properties.natural_language: Gossip-received column data must be from a subnet corresponding to the column's custody group.

reachability.notes: Attacker could publish columns on wrong subnets to confuse custody tracking.

properties.natural_language: Fork activation must be atomic: all Fusaka protocol rules must be applied at the exact activation timestamp, with no partial application.

reachability.notes: Partial fork application would cause consensus splits between clients that applied different subsets of rules.

properties.natural_language: Fork rules must only be applied when block timestamp >= activation timestamp; no early activation is permitted.

reachability.notes: A malicious block proposer could craft a block with manipulated timestamps to trigger premature fork activation, causing a network split.

properties.natural_language: After fork activation, the fork identifier must be updated to the network-specific Fusaka value.

reachability.notes: Incorrect fork ID causes P2P peer discovery failures and network partitioning between clients with different fork IDs.

properties.natural_language: BPO fork timestamps must be strictly ordered: BPO1 < BPO2 < BPO3, and each must be > Fusaka activation timestamp.

reachability.notes: If BPO timestamps are misordered, blob parameter transitions would be applied in wrong order, causing consensus failures.

properties.natural_language: After each BPO fork activation, blob parameters must monotonically increase from the previous BPO level.

reachability.notes: Non-monotonic blob parameter changes could cause transactions valid under one BPO level to become invalid under the next.

properties.natural_language: All 11 core EIPs included in Fusaka must be activated simultaneously at the fork boundary; no subset activation is valid.

reachability.notes: Missing EIP activation creates consensus incompatibility between clients.

properties.natural_language: A block received from a P2P peer must have its RLP-encoded size checked against MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8,388,608 bytes) before any expensive validation.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send blocks exceeding 8 MiB via P2P. If size check occurs after expensive operations (sig verification), this enables resource exhaustion DoS with a single packet.

properties.natural_language: After a block passes the size check (RLP size <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE), it must proceed to further validation steps.

reachability.notes: Valid blocks must not be erroneously rejected by size check.

properties.natural_language: After a block fails the size check (RLP size > MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE), it must be immediately rejected without further processing.

reachability.notes: If oversized blocks are not rejected immediately, they consume processing resources, enabling DoS.

properties.natural_language: MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE (8 MiB) must always be less than the consensus layer MAX_BLOCK_SIZE (10 MiB), maintaining at least a 2 MiB safety margin.

reachability.notes: If the safety margin is violated (e.g., by parameter misconfiguration), blocks valid at EL could be rejected at CL, causing consensus failures.

properties.natural_language: A malicious peer sending an oversized block must be detected and the block rejected before signature verification or state execution.

reachability.notes: Single malicious P2P packet with oversized block. Early rejection prevents resource exhaustion.

properties.natural_language: All client implementations must enforce the same MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE value (8,388,608 bytes) to prevent consensus divergence.

reachability.notes: Different size limit values across clients would cause network splits where some clients accept a block and others reject it.

properties.natural_language: A finalized block ready for propagation must have RLP-encoded size <= MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.

reachability.notes: A locally constructed block exceeding the limit would be rejected by all peers, wasting the validator's block production slot.

properties.natural_language: During block construction, adding a transaction must not cause the projected block RLP size to exceed MAX_RLP_BLOCK_SIZE.

reachability.notes: Size estimation errors during construction could produce oversized blocks.

properties.natural_language: The cell_mask field in NewPooledTransactionHashes (0x08) must be nil when the batch contains no type-3 transactions, or a valid B_16 bitmap otherwise.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send malformed cell_mask in transaction announcements to cause parsing errors or incorrect provider/sampler decisions.

properties.natural_language: GetCells (0x12) requests must contain valid transaction hashes and a valid cell_mask bitmap.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send malformed GetCells requests to cause parsing errors or trigger excessive lookups.

properties.natural_language: Cells (0x13) responses must contain valid cell data matching the requested hashes and columns, validated per EIP-7594 KZG specifications.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send forged cell data in Cells responses. Without KZG validation, fake blob data could enter the mempool.

properties.natural_language: PooledTransactions (0x10) responses with elided blob payloads (RLP nil literals) must be correctly parsed without treating nil as valid blob data.

reachability.notes: Attacker could craft PooledTransactions with malformed nil literals to cause deserialization bugs or type confusion.

properties.natural_language: The probabilistic role decision must use probability p=0.15 for provider role; deviations would affect network-wide data availability.

reachability.notes: If probability is incorrect (e.g., always 0 or 1), the network has either no providers or no samplers, breaking data availability.

properties.natural_language: A sampler must observe at least 2 distinct provider announcements before requesting cells from providers.

reachability.notes: If a sampler requests from a single provider, that provider can selectively withhold data. Requiring 2+ providers adds redundancy.

properties.natural_language: Cell requests must include custody-aligned columns plus C_extra=1 random noise column, with total columns per request <= C_req=8.

reachability.notes: Without noise column, selective withholding detection fails. Exceeding C_req could cause protocol violations.

properties.natural_language: After blob data validation passes per EIP-7594, the transaction must be added to the local mempool and announced to peers.

reachability.notes: If validated transactions are not properly pooled and announced, transaction propagation stalls.

properties.natural_language: A provider must announce with all-ones cell_mask; a sampler must propagate based only on columns it actually possesses.

validation_layers: Cell mask validation by receiving peers
reachability.notes: Attacker claiming all-ones cell_mask without having full data can cause downstream samplers to request cells that don't exist.

properties.natural_language: A noise column in a cell request must be randomly selected from outside the node's custody set to prevent provider from predicting which column is the probe.

reachability.notes: If noise column selection is predictable, malicious providers can serve noise columns while withholding custody columns, evading detection.

properties.natural_language: After a provider fails to return the noise column in a Cells response, the peer must be flagged for misbehavior.

reachability.notes: Malicious provider withholding the noise column is a strong signal of selective data withholding attack.

properties.natural_language: After a provider returns the noise column correctly, the response should increase confidence in the provider's honesty.

reachability.notes: Noise validation is probabilistic - a sophisticated attacker could sometimes serve noise while still withholding other columns.

properties.natural_language: After a peer is flagged for repeated misbehavior, it must be considered for disconnection to prevent ongoing data withholding.

reachability.notes: Without disconnection, flagged peers can continue withholding data.

properties.natural_language: The total columns requested per GetCells message must not exceed C_req=8.

reachability.notes: A peer sending GetCells requesting more than C_req columns should be rejected to prevent amplification attacks.

properties.natural_language: A provider that fetches full blob data must validate it per EIP-7594 before announcing availability.

reachability.notes: Provider announcing invalid data causes downstream samplers to accept corrupted blobs.

properties.natural_language: Block builders using optimistic or proactive blob inclusion policies must not include blobs that have not been successfully sampled or re-sampled.

reachability.notes: Including unsampled blobs in blocks could cause blocks to be rejected by other validators who cannot verify data availability.

properties.natural_language: Conservative blob inclusion policy must only include blobs with full local data availability, never partially sampled blobs.

reachability.notes: Conservative mode including partially available blobs would violate its safety guarantees.

properties.natural_language: The validation pipeline for DataColumnSidecars must be strictly ordered: format check -> inclusion proof -> KZG cell proofs. Skipping any step is a security violation.

reachability.notes: If validation steps are reordered or skipped, computationally expensive KZG verification could be triggered on malformed data (DoS), or invalid data could bypass checks.

properties.natural_language: GetPooledTransactions (0x09) request parsing must validate transaction hash list length and format before processing.

reachability.notes: Attacker can send oversized hash lists in GetPooledTransactions to cause memory exhaustion.

properties.natural_language: Cells response (0x13) must only contain cells for hashes that were requested in the corresponding GetCells (0x12).

reachability.notes: A malicious peer could return cells for unrequested hashes to inject poisoned data.

properties.natural_language: Blob transaction data fetched by a provider via devp2p must be validated before the provider serves cells to samplers.

reachability.notes: If provider accepts invalid blob data from announcing peer and serves it to samplers, invalid data propagates through the network.

properties.natural_language: An attacker controlling fewer than 50% of columns for a block cannot prevent honest nodes from reconstructing the full matrix.

reachability.notes: This is the core security guarantee of erasure coding. If the 50% threshold is insufficient or implementation has off-by-one errors, reconstruction fails.

properties.natural_language: Sybil resistance of custody assignment must hold: manipulating node_id should not allow an attacker to concentrate custody over specific columns disproportionately.

reachability.notes: Attacker generating many node IDs targeting specific custody groups could dominate those columns, then withhold data to break reconstruction for targeted blobs.

properties.natural_language: The threat model for selective withholding and eclipse attacks must be addressed; currently marked as TBD, this represents an open risk.

reachability.notes: Selective withholding and eclipse attack mitigations are incomplete (TBD in spec). An attacker eclipsing a node's provider set could withhold all blob data for specific transactions.

properties.natural_language: Replace-by-fee interactions with sparse blobpool must not cause inconsistent transaction propagation across the network.

reachability.notes: RBF interactions with sparse blobpool are marked TBD. Replaced blob transactions may cause providers and samplers to hold different versions, causing validation failures.

properties.natural_language: EIP-7600 and EIP-7723 dependency requirements must be satisfied before Fusaka activation.

reachability.notes: Missing dependency EIPs could cause undefined behavior at fork activation.

properties.natural_language: The RLP encoding used for size measurement must be canonical and consistent with the encoding used for block hash computation.

reachability.notes: Non-canonical RLP encoding could yield different sizes for the same block across clients, causing consensus divergence.

properties.natural_language: A sampler requesting cells must verify that the responding peer was actually observed as a provider (all-ones cell_mask) before trusting the response.

reachability.notes: If a node accepts cell responses from non-providers, attackers can inject cells without having been verified as providers.
